question: For cross-replica invalidation, compare Redis pub/sub (what cache-kit uses), Redis Streams and RESP3 client-side caching (CLIENT TRACKING). Why pub/sub here, and what would make you switch?
answer_hinglish:
cache-kit pub/sub use karta hai: `set`/`delete` ke baad `PUBLISH` channel par `[instanceId, key]`, har replica ka subscriber key L1 se drop karta hai, sender apna message `id` se ignore karta hai. Channel default `prefix + "invalidate"`.

Pub/sub: simplest. Koi state nahi, koi consumer bookkeeping nahi. Kamzori: fire-and-forget -- disconnected subscriber messages kho deta hai. cache-kit ka mitigation: reconnect (confirmed SUBSCRIBE) par poora L1 clear, aur short L1 TTL as safety net. Half-open connection sirf TTL se bounded.

Redis Streams: durable log. Har replica apni last-read ID yaad rakhe aur reconnect par wahan se replay kare -- toh missed invalidations bhi mil jaate, poora L1 clear nahi karna padta. PLAN: 'durable but needs consumer bookkeeping per replica' -- har replica ka offset, stream ki trimming (MAXLEN), aur naya replica kahan se start kare. Zyada moving parts.

RESP3 CLIENT TRACKING: Redis khud yaad rakhta hai kis client ne kaunsi key padhi, aur key badalne par usko invalidation push karta hai. App ko publish karna hi nahi padta -- koi bhi write (doosre app se bhi) invalidate karta hai. PLAN: 'needs RESP3 and a client that supports it'; README: ioredis 5 ka default RESP2 hai. Tracking ki apni memory cost aur reconnect semantics bhi hain.

Teeno mein se Streams aur CLIENT TRACKING dono 'NOT implemented' hain. Switch kab: agar L1 TTL lamba rakhna zaroori ho (reconnect par full clear mehenga ho) -> Streams. Agar Redis ko doosre services bhi likhte hain jo cache-kit ka publish nahi karte -> tracking, kyunki pub/sub sirf cache-kit ke apne `set`/`delete` ko cover karta hai. Redis Cluster par classic pub/sub saare nodes par broadcast hota hai (generic Redis knowledge) -- yahan cluster test nahi hua.
why_needed: Invalidation transport cache consistency ki reedh ki haddi hai. Har option ka failure mode alag hai, aur galat choice ya toh complexity ya chupi hui staleness laati hai.
real_world_analogy: Pub/sub = loudspeaker announcement (jo nahi sun raha, chook gaya). Streams = notice board register (wapas aake padh sakte ho). Tracking = har customer ka personal SMS jab uska order badle -- dukaan yaad rakhti hai kisne kya liya.
how_it_works: Push invalidation ke teen models: at-most-once broadcast (pub/sub), at-least-once log with consumer offsets (Streams), server-side read tracking with push (CLIENT TRACKING).
in_this_project: `src/two-level.ts`: `invalidateOthers` (`JSON.stringify([this.id, key])`), `onMessage` (malformed message -> `l2-error` op `message`, apna `id` ignore), `onResubscribed` (L1 clear). `L2Subscriber` interface itna chhota hai (ek `subscribe`) ki Streams-based subscriber bhi usi interface ke peeche likha ja sakta tha -- par woh NOT implemented hai. README 'NOT implemented': RESP3 client-side caching, Streams instead of pub/sub, Redis Cluster / Sentinel specifics.
advantages: Pub/sub: zero state, chhota adapter
Message format simple aur validated
Interface itna chhota ki transport badalna possible
disadvantages: Message loss ka sirf blunt fix (full L1 clear)
Sirf cache-kit ke writes invalidate hote hain, Redis ke doosre writers nahi
Har replica ko ek extra connection
common_mistakes: Pub/sub ko queue samajhna
Streams ko 'bas reliable pub/sub' samajhna -- offsets aur trimming bhoolna
Tracking ko RESP2 client ke saath expect karna
follow_up_questions: Streams-based subscriber `L2Subscriber` ke peeche kaise likhoge?
Sharded pub/sub (Redis 7) cluster mein kya badalta hai?
Tracking ki memory cost Redis par kaise control hoti hai?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Pub/sub simplicity vs Streams durability vs tracking automation. cache-kit ne pub/sub + TTL safety net choose kiya kyunki 'bring your own client' aur chhote interfaces goal the.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Pub/sub: disconnect/half-open par lost messages. Streams: consumer lag, trimming se purane entries gaye toh replay incomplete. Tracking: client reconnect par tracking state reset, invalidation flood on mass writes.
advanced.alternatives: DB CDC (binlog) se invalidations, message broker (Kafka) topic, ya cache hi na rakhna critical data ke liye.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Replicas 10x: pub/sub fan-out 10x per write, Redis ke liye usually sasta. Writes 100x: invalidation traffic aur L1 churn badhega; batching ya coarse invalidation (prefix) sochna padega -- jo yahan nahi hai.
advanced.production_improvements: Invalidation lag metric, publish failures par alert (`set`/`delete` false), aur agar Redis ke doosre writers hain toh ya toh woh bhi publish karein ya tracking/CDC par move karo.
